limitations: Microbenchmarks measure timer syscall/control costs, not whole Firefox responsiveness or all signal sources.

Deadline-reset notification benchmark arms real SIGEV_THREAD_ID timers far in the future, so it measures index/target management rather than interrupt-delivery latency. Actual expiry/handler behavior is checked separately.
Darwin has no Linux POSIX timer API. Native Linux is an ARM VM reference, not a same-ABI bare-host Darwin score.
Default stop/termination, process lifecycle and legacy signalfd/sigwait waits retain their real boundaries. CPU-clock POSIX timers and ITIMER_VIRTUAL/PROF are not introduced.
The original POSIX timer metadata bound remains 32 entries; interval timer state is process-owned and retained when disarmed. This does not charge reserved guest RAM.

Earlier same-runtime samples before adding the notification-path benchmark remain in target/timers/perf and solo-recheck; the final record uses the exact final fixture SHA for primary/native/long-solo results.
The no-timer recheck used the same accepted runtime source before the paired Git metadata rebuild; diagnostic code is unchanged.
